verses.text: Moses went and said these words to all Israel.
“I'm 120 years old today. I can't go out and come in anymore. The LORD has told me, ‘You won't cross this Jordan.’
The LORD your God himself will cross ahead of you. He'll destroy these nations before you, and you'll take possession of their land. Joshua will cross ahead of you, just as the LORD said.
The LORD will do to them what he did to Sihon and Og, the Amorite kings, and to their land when he destroyed them.
The LORD will hand them over to you, and you'll deal with them according to every command I've given you.
Be strong and brave. Don't let them scare or terrify you, because the LORD your God himself goes with you. He won't fail you or leave you.”

Moses called Joshua and said in front of all Israel, “Be strong and brave. You're going with these people into the land the LORD swore to give their ancestors, and you'll lead them into their inheritance.
The LORD himself goes ahead of you. He'll be with you and won't fail you or leave you. Don't be afraid. Don't lose heart.”
Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests from the tribe of Levi who carried the ark of the LORD's covenant, and to all the elders of Israel.
Moses gave them this command: “At the end of every seven years, at the appointed time in the year of release, during the Festival of Booths,
when all Israel comes to appear before the LORD your God at the place he chooses, read this law out loud so everyone can hear.
Bring everyone together: men, women, children, and the foreigners in your towns. Let them hear and learn to honor the LORD your God and carefully follow every word of this law.
Then their children who haven't learned it yet will hear and learn to honor the LORD your God for as long as you live in the land you're crossing the Jordan to take as your own.”

The LORD said to Moses, “Your time to die is near. Call Joshua and come with him to the Tent of Meeting so I can commission him.” So Moses and Joshua went and presented themselves at the Tent of Meeting.
The LORD appeared at the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar stood over the entrance.

The LORD told Moses, “You'll soon die and rest with your ancestors. These people will be unfaithful to me and chase after the foreign gods of the land they're entering. They'll abandon me and break the covenant I made with them.

Then my anger will flare up against them. I'll abandon them and hide my face from them. They'll be devoured, and all sorts of trouble and disaster will come upon them. Then they'll say, ‘Aren't these disasters happening because our God isn't with us?’
I will certainly hide my face that day because of all the evil they've done by turning to other gods.
So write down this song for yourselves and teach it to the Israelites. Put it on their lips, so the song can be my witness against them.

I'll bring them into the land flowing with milk and honey that I swore to give their ancestors. They'll eat their fill and grow fat. Then they'll turn to other gods and serve them, treat me with contempt, and break my covenant.

When all sorts of trouble and disaster come upon them, this song will testify as a witness before them. Their descendants will still remember its words. I know the direction they're headed and what they're doing today, before I've even brought them into the land I promised them.”
That same day Moses wrote down the song and taught it to the Israelites.
The LORD commissioned Joshua son of Nun and said, “Be strong and brave. You'll bring the Israelites into the land I swore to give them. I'll be with you.”
When Moses had finished writing every word of this law in a book,
he gave this command to the Levites who carried the ark of the LORD's covenant:
“Take this book of the law and put it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God. Keep it there as a witness against you.
I know how rebellious and stubborn you are. You've rebelled against the LORD while I'm still alive here with you. How much more will you rebel after I'm gone?
Bring all your tribal elders and officers to me. I'll say these words so they can hear them, and I'll call heaven and earth as witnesses against them.

I know that after I die you'll completely corrupt yourselves and turn away from the path I told you to follow. In the days to come, disaster will reach you because you'll do evil in the LORD's sight and stir up his anger with what your hands have made.”
Then Moses recited every word of this song so the whole assembly of Israel could hear it.
